title: Constructibility of module sheaves descends along qcqs surjections
statement: Let $a:T\to U$ be a surjective morphism [def-weil-surjective-morphism] of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and $G$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. If $a^{-1}G$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], then $G$ is constructible in the same finite constructible-stratification sense.

source.place: Tag 095Q, label lemma-check-constructible, part (3), converse for finite coefficient rings

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-surjective-pullback] with $u=a$, $V=T$, $U=U$, and $F=G$. Its hypotheses are exactly that $a$ is surjective, $T$ and $U$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $\Lambda$ is a finite commutative ring, and $G$ is a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $U_{\Et}$, all of which are assumptions here. It gives $G$ constructible if and only if $a^{-1}G$ constructible, with constructibility defined by the same node def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf. The reverse implication applied to the assumed constructibility of $a^{-1}G$ proves the claim.
